quizzes.question: Java always passes arguments using the Pass-by-Value method.
quizzes.explanation:
Java always uses pass-by-value.
For primitives, a copy of the value is passed; for reference types, a copy of the reference value (address) is passed.

quizzes.question: Changing the value of a primitive parameter inside a method also changes the caller's original value.
quizzes.explanation: A copy of the value is passed for primitives, so changes inside the method do not affect the original.

quizzes.question: Modifying an object's properties inside a method is reflected in the caller's original object.
quizzes.explanation:
A copy of the reference value is passed, but since it points to the same object, property changes are reflected in the original.
However, reassigning the reference itself does not affect the original.

quizzes.question: Assigning a new object to a parameter inside a method also changes the caller's reference.
quizzes.explanation:
Since a copy of the reference value is passed, assigning a new object to the parameter does not affect the original reference.
This is the core of Pass-by-Value.

quizzes.question: Passing an object in Java is Pass-by-Reference.
quizzes.explanation:
This is a common misconception.
Java passes the 'reference value' 'by value' (Pass-by-Value of Reference).
True Pass-by-Reference, like C++'s & reference, passes the original variable itself.

quizzes.question: A swap(a, b) method can exchange the values of two primitive variables.
quizzes.explanation:
Since Java is Pass-by-Value, swapping the parameters inside the method does not change the original variables.
You must use arrays or objects as a workaround.

quizzes.question: When a String is passed to a method, modifications made inside the method are reflected in the caller.
quizzes.explanation:
String is an immutable object, so it is not 'modified' but rather a new String object is created.
Even if the parameter points to a new object, the original reference remains unchanged.

quizzes.question: When an array is passed to a method, its elements can be modified inside the method.
quizzes.explanation:
Since arrays are objects, the reference value is copied and passed.
Because it points to the same array, element changes are reflected in the caller.

quizzes.question: C++ references (&) and Java references are identical concepts.
quizzes.explanation:
A C++ reference (&) is an alias for the original variable, providing true Pass-by-Reference.
A Java reference is an independent variable that holds the address value of an object.

quizzes.question: When a method is called, the arguments are copied into a separate stack frame.
quizzes.explanation:
A new stack frame is created for each method call, and argument values are copied into the parameters.
This is why changes inside a method are not propagated to the caller.
